source.title: Sparse Autoencoders Reveal Temporal Difference Learning in Large Language Models
source.authors: Can Demircan; Tankred Saanum; A. K. Jagadish; Marcel Binz; Eric Schulz

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether SAEs can recover meaningful sparse features from an LLM's representations, including by intervening on recovered features. This is a conceptual test of V4, not a reproduction of the toy-model superposition experiments.
record.gate_note: The paper's in-context task performance and behavioral-model comparisons are not included unless tied to an SAE feature intervention. Results cited from other work are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study uses SAEs as a tool to find TD-error, Q-value and successor-representation correlates in Llama 3 70B during in-context RL, and lesions those latents. It never tests whether features are superposed, spread across neurons, or whether an SAE recovers the model's features in general. Sparse L0 counts and task-variable correlations are outputs of the tool, not a test of V4. No version is tested, so the rows are relinked to none.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that Llama 3 70B implements TD-like learning in-context, with SAE latents matching TD errors, Q-values and the SR, and that lesioning or clamping them causally changes behaviour and representations. They note the SAEs are task-specific and that replication with other LLMs is needed. They make no claim about superposition.
record.recipe_differences: The paper applies task-specific SAEs to Llama residual-stream activations and tests correlations and causal interventions; it does not use the original toy-model feature-geometry setup or measure superposition geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: The SAE analyses are task-specific. In the Community Graph task, the reported L0 profile rises again toward the last blocks, unlike its tendency to peak in middle blocks in the Two-Step and Grid World tasks.

fits_no_version.finding: Task-specific SAE latents in Llama 3 70B correlate with TD errors (max r=0.58 to 0.60) and Q-values. Zeroing them degrades RL behaviour and later representations, while control lesions barely matter.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE latents in LLMs can isolate causally relevant in-context learning signals (TD errors) whose ablation alters behaviour.

fits_no_version.finding: Task-specific SAEs on 8192-d residual streams have L0 of at most about 30 active latents, peaking mid-network.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Task-restricted LLM activations admit very sparse SAE codes.

record.problems: Only Llama 3 70B is used for the main SAE analyses, with Llama 3 8B included for a behavioral scale comparison. SAEs are task-specific, the paper states that their findings do not establish generality across tasks or LLMs, and several intervention outcomes are reported qualitatively or in figures without numerical values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No result-bearing SAE-feature findings were omitted. Standalone task-performance and behavioral-model results were left out because they do not measure SAE feature recovery or feature geometry.

untested.parts: All: no toy models, geometry or sparsity transition.
All: polysemanticity is cited only as motivation.
Whether features are spread across neurons, and whether SAEs recover the model's sparse features. SAEs are used as an analysis tool only.
All: no completeness, stability or canonicity tests.

record.verdict_notes: The record lists peer_reviewed as ICLR, but the supplied text (v1) is marked 'Preprint. Under review.' This should be verified. The reader's V4 'supports' labels should be dropped: the paper treats SAEs as an assumed tool, not as an object of test.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not test feature overlap, near-orthogonal geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, or regular geometry in toy networks.
It mentions polysemanticity as motivation for SAEs but does not test capacity competition or dedicated versus shared dimensions.
It does not test whether polysemantic neurons can arise without capacity pressure.
Evidence is from task-specific SAEs and in-context RL tasks in Llama 3 70B; it does not establish how broadly features are distributed across neurons in LLMs generally.
The paper does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units of the model.
It does not compare one-dimensional feature directions with multidimensional features.

rows.subject: Llama 3 70B
rows.operation_detail: Correlated SAE latents with Q-learning TD errors in the Two-Step Task.
rows.measure: Maximum correlation between an SAE feature and the Q-learning TD error
rows.note: The authors identify this as the highest-correlation TD feature.
rows.check: The max correlation of an SAE latent with Q-learning TD error (r=0.58) is a finding about TD-like computation, not about whether features are superposed or distributed.

rows.subject: Llama 3 70B
rows.operation_detail: Compared the block 34 SAE feature time course qualitatively with TD errors.

conditions.value: Two-Step Task, standard and reward- and transition-disruption variations

rows.measure: Qualitative correspondence of SAE feature activity with TD-error changes
rows.value: The SAE feature shows similar changes when reward or transition dynamics change.
rows.note: The figure shows six runs across the three task variations.
rows.check: A qualitative TD-error match does not bear on any superposition version.

rows.subject: Llama 3 70B
rows.operation_detail: Set the block 34 TD SAE latent to zero and reconstructed the residual stream before choices.
rows.value: Significantly worse performance; numerical values not stated in text.
rows.note: The text reports a significant impairment but does not give the plotted values.
rows.check: The lesion effect on task return shows the latent's causal role in RL, not superposition. The values are figure-only.

rows.subject: Llama 3 70B
rows.operation_detail: Deactivated the block 34 SAE feature with the lowest correlation to TD.
rows.measure: Behavioral likelihood under the Q-learning model
rows.value: The lesion did not make behavior less likely according to the Q-learning model.
rows.check: This is a control lesion for the RL finding.

rows.subject: Llama 3 70B
rows.operation_detail: Clamped the block 34 TD latent to -10.
rows.measure: Subsequent SAE-latent correlations with Q-values and TD errors
rows.value: The correlation strengths for both Q-values and TD errors decreased substantially; numerical values not stated in text.
rows.note: The text describes a substantial decrease but gives no plotted values.
rows.check: The clamp effect on later correlations concerns the TD mechanism, not superposition.

rows.subject: Llama 3 70B
rows.operation_detail: Correlated SAE latents with Q-values of the agent that generated the observations.
rows.baseline: Correlations with estimates from a Q-learning agent trained on randomized rewards were also examined.
rows.value: The highest correlations throughout the transformer blocks were with the Q-values used to generate the observations; numerical values not stated in text.
rows.uncertainty: 95% confidence intervals are shown in Figure 5, but values are not stated in text.
rows.note: The paper reports the comparison in text; the plotted numerical values are not transcribed.
rows.check: Q-value correlations in Grid World are about the RL mechanism.

rows.subject: Llama 3 70B
rows.operation_detail: Correlated SAE latents with TD errors of the agent that generated the observations.
rows.measure: SAE-latent correlations with generating-agent TD errors
rows.baseline: Correlations with estimates from a Q-learning agent trained on randomized rewards were also examined.
rows.value: Most blocks showed the highest correlations with TD errors from the generating model; numerical values not stated in text.
rows.uncertainty: 95% confidence intervals are shown in Figure 5, but values are not stated in text.
rows.note: The paper also reports high correlations with myopic error signals.
rows.check: TD-error correlations in Grid World are about the RL mechanism.

rows.subject: Llama 3 70B
rows.operation_detail: Set four selected TD-correlated SAE latents to zero.

conditions.value: four latents across four blocks, selected from block 40 onward with r ≥ 0.75 to TD errors

rows.measure: Accuracy in predicting the Q-learning agent's actions
rows.value: Lesioning the TD latents significantly degraded action prediction; numerical values not stated in text.
rows.note: The text reports significant degradation but does not provide the plotted values.
rows.check: This is a lesion effect on action prediction. The latents were selected with r≥0.75, which is a selection criterion.

rows.subject: Llama 3 70B
rows.operation_detail: Lesioned the lowest-correlation latents from the same blocks as the TD-latent lesions.

conditions.value: latents with lowest TD-error correlations in the selected blocks

rows.measure: Accuracy in predicting the Q-learning agent's actions
rows.value: Only very small changes in action predictions.
rows.check: This is a control lesion for the RL finding.

rows.subject: Llama 3 70B
rows.operation_detail: Compared SAE-latent correlations with successor-representation and transition-matrix representations.
rows.measure: Maximum correlation with the corresponding learned representation
rows.uncertainty: 95% confidence intervals are shown in Figure 5, but values are not stated in text.
rows.note: The paper states that SAE-latent correlations were stronger for the successor representation than for the transition matrix.
rows.check: The SR vs transition-matrix comparison tests TD vs model-based learning, not superposition.

rows.subject: Llama 3 70B
rows.operation_detail: Compared SAE-latent correlations with TD errors for successor-representation learning and with transition-model surprise.
rows.measure: Maximum correlation with the corresponding learning signal
rows.uncertainty: 95% confidence intervals are shown in Figure 5, but values are not stated in text.
rows.note: The paper reports substantially stronger correlation with the TD error.
rows.check: The TD-error vs surprise comparison concerns the learning mechanism.

rows.subject: Llama 3 70B
rows.operation_detail: Deactivated the TD latent with the strongest TD-error correlation in block 64.
rows.measure: Accuracy in predicting the next state
rows.uncertainty: 95% confidence intervals are shown in Figure 6, but values are not stated in text.
rows.note: The text gives the accuracy before and after the lesion.
rows.check: This is a lesion effect on next-state accuracy (24.3% to 18.9%). The baseline 24.3% is also reported as the overall mean accuracy (ceiling 25%).

rows.subject: Llama 3 70B
rows.operation_detail: Deactivated the block 64 TD latent and measured subsequent SAE-latent correlations.
rows.measure: Correlation of subsequent SAE latents with the successor representation
rows.value: Correlation was reduced; numerical values not stated in text.
rows.uncertainty: 95% confidence intervals are shown in Figure 6, but values are not stated in text.
rows.note: The text says the reduction persisted despite recovery of TD correlations.
rows.check: This is a lesion effect on SR correlations, the RL mechanism.

rows.subject: Llama 3 70B
rows.operation_detail: Deactivated the block 64 TD latent and measured subsequent SAE-latent correlations.
rows.measure: Correlation of subsequent SAE latents with TD errors
rows.value: TD correlations recovered rapidly after the lesion; numerical values not stated in text.
rows.uncertainty: 95% confidence intervals are shown in Figure 6, but values are not stated in text.
rows.note: The paper describes recovery after the intervention.
rows.check: This describes TD-correlation recovery after the lesion.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Task-specific SAE analyses of Llama 3 70B in the Two-Step Task, Grid World, and Community Graph
reader_labels.reason: SAE latents track task-relevant TD, Q-value, or successor-representation signals, and interventions on selected latents alter behavior or subsequent representations (r1-r3, r5-r8, r10-r14).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: SAE activity profiles across the three studied tasks
reader_labels.reason: The authors report that the 8192-dimensional residual stream is represented with a few dozen active SAE features (r15-r17).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: The studied task-specific SAE analyses in Llama 3 70B
reader_labels.reason: The evidence is task-specific and the authors state that the SAEs are not suitable for identifying RL-related variables in arbitrary tasks; generality across LLMs remains untested (r1-r17).
